evidence.excerpt: Build the inventory service from this repository
A training project: build a REST API for warehouse inventory.
- Expose create, read, update and delete endpoints for items under /api/items.
- Authenticate every request with JWT bearer tokens.
- Store data in PostgreSQL and manage the schema with migrations.
- Paginate list endpoints at 20 items per page.
- Integration tests cover every endpoint.
- The whole service starts with `docker compose up`.
- OpenAPI documentation for the endpoints.
Languages: JavaScript, PLpgSQL
Repository paths: package.json, src/app.js, src/routes/items.js, src/middleware/auth.js, migrations/001_init.sql, test/items.test.js, docker-compose.yml, README.md

assumptions: Tests referenced by the acceptance criteria will be integration tests run by a Node.js test runner (exact runner not specified in provided sources).
JWT token format (claims, signing algorithm, secret management) is not specified in the sources and will need to be defined by implementers.

Database connection details (host, port, user, password) and how docker-compose wires services together are not specified in the excerpts and must be derived from docker-compose.yml and environment variables at implementation time.
The provided migrations/001_init.sql is the expected starting migration for schema management, but its contents were not supplied in the excerpts.
The test file test/items.test.js exists and may encode additional behavioral expectations; its content was not provided and thus exact test expectations are unknown.

requirements.statement: Build the inventory service from this repository.
Expose create, read, update and delete endpoints for items under /api/items.
Authenticate every request with JWT bearer tokens.
Store data in PostgreSQL and manage the schema with migrations.
Paginate list endpoints at 20 items per page.
Integration tests cover every endpoint.
The whole service starts with `docker compose up`.
Provide OpenAPI documentation for the endpoints (nice to have).
Use JavaScript and PLpgSQL (repository languages) for implementation.

Repository contains these paths which should be preserved/used: package.json, src/app.js, src/routes/items.js, src/middleware/auth.js, migrations/001_init.sql, test/items.test.js, docker-compose.yml, README.md.
